$comment: Root ADR-0177. What the staging smoke runs on a new release before production switches to it, and how long each step may take. scripts/ops/staging-smoke.sh is the only reader; scripts/deploy/foundation-release.sh `staging-smoke` starts it (between the admission build and the release switch of scripts/deploy/foundation-deploy.sh) and bounds the whole run by unit_limit_seconds. The staging key prefix lives in the R2 client (R2KeyNamespace, crates/foundation-outbox) and the staging database name in scripts/ops/database-url.sh; neither is restated here. It asks no provider (root ADR-0363, amended 2026-11-27): its plan, ingest and measure steps read the hub and VWorld sites live until then, and VWorld's scheduled maintenance of 2026-11-27 refused five releases in a row.
unit_limit_reason: The migrator image build (up to an hour on a cold cache, the same build the release's `migrate` step runs a few minutes later and then finds cached) plus the smoke itself (target under ten minutes) plus margin. orchestration/tests/test_deploy_started_once.py holds foundation-autodeploy.service's TimeoutStartSec above the deploy's waits plus this.
unit_memory_reason: The publisher's plan, inventory, streaming ingest and ranged member reads, measured in production at well under 1 GiB; no Spark, DuckDB or tile work runs here. The host's budget (tools/host-memory-budget.contract.json) counts this as host_reserved, and the deploy runs it while every registered job is drained.

clear.what: empty the staging/ namespace: every run starts from an empty staging/, and staging never holds more than one run

image.what: build the release's runtime image (the migrator) under a staging tag

database.what: drop and create foundation_staging, then the release's bootstrap, migrations, grants and finalize: the schema chain from empty

retention: one run: each smoke empties staging/ and recreates foundation_staging before it starts, so the last run's objects and rows stay for inspection until the next deploy and never accumulate.
